title: feature-team-slo-collaboration-worklog-and-decision-diary-2026
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working log for cross-functional coordination between feature teams, platform, and SRE to define, test, and operationalize SLOs for model-serving surfaces (hosted API, dedicated pools, private deployments). Unlike the official playbook, this is a scratchpad + decision diary capturing trade-offs, experiment outcomes, and immediate action items.

Scope:
- Focused on latency and correctness SLOs for the text-generation/chat endpoints and embeddings pipeline.
- Includes canary rollouts, canary metrics, runbook handoffs, and error-budget experiments.
- Excludes long-term governance cadence (will be handed to Reliability Governance after Q2 pilot).

Key stakeholders (working group):
- Product: Priya Nair (hosted-api PM)
- Eng - Serving Runtime: Diego Alvarez
- Platform Engineering: Samir Patel
- Observability / Console: Lina Gómez
- SRE Lead (owner): Maya Chen
- Solutions / CS review: Ash Thomas (ad-hoc)

High-level goals (Q1–Q2 sprint runway):
1) Define service-level indicators (SLIs) and concretely measure them across 3 regions for the next 6 weeks.
2) Run 90-day error-budget experiments for the hosted-chat route and one dedicated model route.
3) Deliver runbooks and handoff package for oncall teams + a canary rollback policy.
4) Produce a short exec one-pager with cost/latency tradeoffs and proposal for SLO targets.

Initial SLI proposals (working):
- P99 end-to-end server latency (generation completion) for chat: target 350ms (adjust per-model).
- P95 model latency for small models (<4B tokens context): 120ms.
- Successful-response rate (500/502): 99.8% per 30d window.
- Regret metric (eval set prompt->model delta) for quality regressions: <1.5% regression compared to baseline.

Data & instrumentation checklist (to validate before baseline week):
- Route tagging: ensure all requests carry route_id, model_version, region, customer_tier (PR: #412).
- Distributed traces enabled (sampling 10% with 100% error trace retention for timeouts).
- Synthetic canary traffic harness (locally reproducible, runs every 5m).
- Error-budget burn-rate dashboards (per-route and aggregated).
- Alerts: slow_p99 (>target by 50ms sustained for 10m), increased 5xx rate (>0.2% over baseline), quality-regression alert from eval pipeline.

Weekly worklog (selected entries):
- 2026-01-12 (kickoff): Draft goals and SLIs. Agreed to a 6-week baseline measurement period. Action: Diego to add route tags to runtime (REL-234).
- 2026-01-20: First synthetic canary runs; observed regional variance in P99 (us-west ~25% higher). Hypothesis: autoscaler config + network egress. Action: Samir to validate autoscaler breakpoints by 2026-01-27.
- 2026-01-28: Decision: keep initial SLO targets but add region-specific adjustment band. Rationale: avoid premature alerts while we gather more data. Logged as DEC-01.
- 2026-02-03: Observability team added error budget dashboard to console (alpha). Noted gaps in per-customer breakdown—Priya to prioritize top 5 enterprise customers for additional telemetry.
- 2026-02-10: Ran controlled degradation test (throttle KV cache miss rate). Result: P99 degraded ~2.3x under 30% forced miss. Conclusion: prioritize KV cache instrumentation and fallback policy. Action: Diego + runtime team to implement cache hit metrics and soft-fallback by 2026-02-24.
- 2026-02-18: Canary rollback runbook draft reviewed. Missing: escalation path when quality-regression alert fires. Action: Lina to draft quality alert steps and contact list.

Decision log (concise):
- DEC-01 (2026-01-28): Use region-adjusted SLO bands (no single global SLO for first pilot). Owners: Maya / Priya.
- DEC-02 (2026-02-05): Canary window set to 30m with 15m warm-up, synthetic workload matching 75th percentile of production QPS. Owner: Samir.
- DEC-03 (2026-02-11): Quality regressions will trigger immediate canary pause + auto-fallback to previous model version. Owner: Diego.

Experiment matrix (planned):
- Experiment A: Autoscaler breakpoint tuning (small burst vs steady). Metric: P95/P99 + queue length. Window: 2 weeks. Owner: Samir.
- Experiment B: KV cache miss soft-fallback (serve from quantized backup model when miss>threshold). Metric: perceived latency + token cost delta + quality regressions. Window: 3 weeks. Owner: Diego.
- Experiment C: Canary traffic profile sensitivity (75% vs 90% traffic match). Metric: false positive rate for rollbacks. Owner: Priya.

Runbook / handoff requirements (minimum deliverables):
- Playbook: step-by-step rollback, throttling, and mitigation flows (for oncall).
- Runbook snippets per route: owner, escalation list, quick mitigations.
- Short training session: 30m for oncall to walk through playbook and the canary dashboard.

Immediate action items (current):
- Diego: add per-request route tagging and cache-hit instrumentation (due 2026-02-24).
- Samir: run autoscaler breakpoint experiment and report (due 2026-02-21).
- Lina: complete quality-regression alert playbook and contact list (due 2026-02-22).
- Priya: prioritize top-5 customers for telemetry and confirm privacy constraints (due 2026-02-26).
- Maya: prepare executive one-pager with cost/latency tradeoffs for 2026-03-01.

Risks & notes (raw):
- Inconsistent route tagging will poison dashboards — high priority to fix.
- Model-level variability (some models have bursty KV usage) complicates one-size-fits-all SLOs.
- Cost impact: more aggressive canaries and synthetic traffic will increase token spend—need a budget cap.

Open questions (to resolve):
- Q1: Do we allow per-customer SLOs for enterprise customers during pilot, or only route-level SLOs? (Priya to advise legal/data-compliance).
- Q2: What is acceptable manual intervention window for canaries before auto-fallback triggers? (debate between safety vs. human review).

Reference links and ephemeral notes:
- Confluence draft: /display/Reliability/SLO-Blueprint (see instrumentation checklist)
- GitHub PR: serving-runtime#412 adds route_id header
- Jira: REL-234 autoscaler experiment backlog
- Slack: discussion thread #reliability -> threads "canary-window" and "kv-miss-impact"

Next steps (short):
1) Lock instrumentation changes and run baseline week (week of 2026-02-22).
2) Run Experiment A and B in parallel across staging and canary clusters.
3) Prepare runbook drafts and schedule oncall training for 2026-03-08.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep decision log terse. Link to PRs/Jira in the DEC entry.
- When handing to Reliability Governance, include list of experiments + burn-rate outcomes + suggested long-term SLOs.
- Avoid baking in rigid SLO numbers until we have stable 30d windows across regions.

If you're editing this doc: add entries under the weekly worklog with date prefix, and add DEC- numbers for every formal decision. Use Jira keys for experiments.
